column7:
I tend to be flexible with my hourly rate (+/- 10% of what I usually charge). 

If the job is going to be longer term (e.g., months), and the work is going to be guaranteed (e.g., 15+ hours/week), I can budget for a slightly lower rate. Jobs like this are usually more iterative and client-facing. For example, building a complex interactive map dashboard with hundreds of graphs, custom color schemes, and links to large scale data will take longer and require lots of data cleaning and client feedback time, so I'm willing to take a bit of a hit on the hourly rate, because a) the work itself is more time consuming than it is challenging, and b) I know the overall cost of the job will be higher because of time spent. 

I also take into consideration the size of the business/individual I'm working with; for example, if the group is a non-profit or microbusiness, and the difference between $60/hour and $65/hour would make or break the contract, I will also take a hit on the hourly rate if I think the job is worthwhile. 

However, if the job requires more analytical or technical skill, it's important to me to charge accordingly. Developing complex raster models and writing custom scripts to calculate outputs or automate processes in ADDITION to making the maps alone can and should cost more. Also -- if I sense that doing this job will take away from my mental or physical capacity to take on more work, I need to charge the client a rate that takes that into consideration.

I have only been a freelance cartographer for a couple years, and it's the best job I've ever had. Before this, I had worked across the spectrum of the geospatial industry, from defense/intelligence contracting to transportation and utility mapping to field surveying. Being a small business owner didn't even cross my mind until it seemed to land in my lap, and it is certainly a constant learning process -- I will forever be updating my portfolio, changing my hourly rate, and advertising new product/service offerings to see what sticks. I am perpetually shocked and proud of myself for making this career a reality, which is why I'm constantly encouraging others to pursue their own freelance opportunities. 

I just came across the results from your 2022 survey today, and I found it fascinating, so I'm very glad to be able to participate in this years' survey. Even just to know that there are other full-time freelance GIS and cartography folks out there makes me feel less alone in this journey, and I'll be so excited and grateful to see the results! Project-based pricing ensures the client gets what they want and I am fairly compensated. I also ask: Do I like the work? Does it align with my values? What will I need to complete the work? Do I have to learn a new skill? How is the client to work with? What kinds of funds are they working with? Private businesses clients with deep pockets pay 125 an hour which helps to offset the many hours of volunteer work I provide every month to good causes.

column18: Mainly would say that people should bill what they feel they are worth, and use the survey as a guide to make sure they are billing enough (seems like very few people bill "too much"). Also recommend billing fixed fees for projects where possible so you're billing what the project is worth, not the amount of time you took working on. Sometimes you're really efficient and shouldn't penalize yourself by billing less hours than it would typically take. Also billing fixed fee can allow you to be more creative and take risks, or learn a new approach without worrying about if you're billing too many hours to the client.
